head: 2aedd9bce5e7c9e6b2419a72ef916caaa7d946de
summary: Test-only change: a real-thread, real-HTTP, real-PostgreSQL IT with a start gate. It proves exactly K accepted and N-K rejected, exact counters, counters equal to postings and a zero sum per currency. One minor weak assertion: rejections are checked only by HTTP 422.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: assertCountersEqualPostings and assertPostingsSumToZeroPerCurrency in both tests
Outcome is deterministic by construction (fixed K, statuses counted). Author reports 5/5 local runs and 172/172 in the full build (maven-20261019-122551.log).

findings.description: B1 requires the N-K rejections to be 'insufficient funds', but only the HTTP status 422 is counted. Another 422 cause (e.g. a validation error) would pass unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Capture the response body and assert the Problem Details type or code for insufficient funds on every rejected response.

findings.description: The opposing-transfers test is not in the brief. It is cheap and relevant to AC2.5, and a deadlock would surface as a failed request. The comment about sorting by account id is unverified here.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but reference the production lock-ordering code in the comment or drop that claim.
